name: Lipoblast
short_description: Early precursor from a mesenchymal stem cell. Picks up the first small lipid droplets before maturing into a preadipocyte. Key in embryonic fat development; reappear in liposarcomas.

textbook.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; rounded-to-oval cell mid-transition from spindle to round, ~18 small discrete pale lipid droplets in a clean multilocular pattern (never merged), each with a thin darker perilipin rim, nucleus with a clearly scalloped/lobed indented outline and one visible nucleolus, a wavy rough-ER/Golgi patch beside the nucleus, several small elongated mitochondria dispersed among the droplets, muted dusty palette, thin clean outlines, fills the charcoal square edge-to-edge, no baked text, no border)

sem.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; single continuous rounded cell body with an irregular, multiply-bulging/lobed surface where the underlying small lipid droplets visibly push out against the membrane, two short blunt tapering process remnants at one pole hinting at the recent spindle-shaped precursor stage, no internal organelles drawn (surface-only as SEM should show), warm golden-amber false colour against a clean dark uncluttered background, no appendage/second-organism artifacts, no text, no border)
